text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The leaders of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces decided to press on with demands for early general elections and oppose formation of a new Socialist cabinet.
-- The ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party and its parliamentary allies decided that early general elections could be held at the end of 1997.
-- An International Monetary Fund mission is expected to arrive in Bulgaria to resume funding talks only after a new cabinet is in place, an IMF official said.

-- The National Electricity Company, Bulgarian State Railways and other 136 state companies would not be offered for sell-off during 1997 because of their strategic importance for the country's economy, a draft privatisation programme approved by the outgoing cabinet said.

-- Bulgaria expects some $1.2 billion from the privatisation of 27 large state enterprises in 1997 under the draft privatisaion programme, yet to be approved by parliament, outgoing Economy minister Roumen Getchev said.
-- Bulgaria's internal debt rose to 1.052 trillion levs at end-December from 839 billion levs a month earlier, finance ministry and central bank figures showed.
-- Prices of coal and electricity are expected to rise by 37.6 percent from February 1, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
